claim: *Measurement does not imply enforcement.* A sensor produces an observed measurement, which is compared with a declared bound. The result remains report-only unless the evidence warrants a warning or an admission gate.
topology:
A running system is observed along a dashed arrow into a measurement box holding latency, cost,
    and queue depth. The measurement is compared, along a solid arrow, against a declared bound. The comparison
    branches on whether enforcement is warranted. A no leads to a plain report-only box: the number is surfaced,
    not enforced. A yes flows along a heavy bordered arrow, crossed by a gate glyph, into a warning or admission
    gate — the one place enforcement sits. The lesson: represent first; add enforcement only when the evidence
    warrants it. Legend as in Figure C-1; weight, dash, and glyph carry the meaning without colour.
required_terms: A quantity does not earn a gate by being measurable.
bw_encoding: Only the conditional admission gate is lightly shaded; measuring and reporting do not imply enforcement.
redesign: Layout reflowed for a 15 cm monochrome print column; color categories replaced by labels and boundary weight. Fidelity pass: Restored double-bar admission-gate glyph on yes branch; report-only alternative remains unguarded.
alt: Measurement does not imply enforcement — a number earns a gate only when evidence warrants it
